mainTopic: Impure communities and פסח שני, and when the ציץ atones for impurity of the offering, the owner, or the כהן (including טומאת התהום)
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier dispute: does only a פסח brought in טהרה push others off to פסח שני, or does one brought in טומאה do so too? Next, רבי מני בר פטיש rules on a community split into thirds: זבין, people who are pure, and טמאי מתים. The טמאי מתים lose both the first פסח and פסח שני, because the זבין are counted differently for each date. A new משנה then teaches that the ציץ makes up for impurity of the offering's blood or meat, but not for impurity of the person's body. The exception is טומאת התהום, a hidden impurity. The גמרא reads the משנה's wording closely and raises a contradiction from a ברייתא. רבינא and רבי שילא resolve it in two different ways. רמי בר חמא then asks whether the טומאת התהום leniency also covers the כהן. רבא tries to prove from רבי חייא that it does, and רב יוסף rejects the proof. The amud ends with a challenge to רב יוסף from רבי יוסי's ruling about a שומרת יום כנגד יום, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The root of the dispute: does an impure פסח push others to פסח שני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pinpoints the dispute. One view holds that only a פסח brought in טהרה pushes others off to פסח שני. The other view, that of רב אדא בר אהבה, holds that even a פסח brought in טומאה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: One view: a פסח brought in purity pushes others off to the second פסח, but a פסח brought in impurity does not. The other Master holds that even a פסח brought in impurity pushes others off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a discussion on the previous amud. It explains exactly what the two opinions disagree about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a case where part of the community brings the פסח and another part cannot. The question is whether the group that could not is now sent to פסח שני. The first view says this only happens if the first group's פסח was brought in טהרה. רב אדא בר אהבה, who said there is a fix for the people left out, holds that even a פסח brought in טומאה sends the others to פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Pushes off / defers others to פסח שני
Ritual purity: here, a פסח brought by pure people
Ritual impurity: here, a פסח brought in impurity because the majority was impure
"The Master holds": the formula that lays out each side's view

phrases.english: [A Pesach brought in] purity defers [others],
phrases.notes: This is the end of the first opinion's reasoning. Its opening words were in the previous section.

phrases.english: [a Pesach brought in] impurity does not defer [others].
And the [other] Master holds —
phrases.notes: Per Sefaria, this is רב אדא בר אהבה.

phrases.english: even [a Pesach brought in] impurity also defers [others].

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מסקנא (it closes the previous dispute by identifying its root)
steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָר סָבַר — אֲפִילּוּ טוּמְאָה נָמֵי מְדַחֲיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the dispute that began on the previous amud
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement is whether a פסח offered in טומאה, and not only one offered in טהרה, pushes others off to פסח שני.

steps.title: A community split into thirds: רבי מני בר פטיש's ruling
steps.stepSummary: A new case: one third are זבין, one third are pure, and one third are טמאי מתים. רבי מני בר פטיש rules that the טמאי מתים bring neither the first פסח nor פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if a third of the people were זבין, a third were pure, and a third were impure from a dead body, רבי מני בר פטיש said that those impure from a dead body do not bring the פסח on the first date or on the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case and gives רבי מני בר פטיש's ruling. The next two steps will explain his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if most of the community is טמא מת, they bring the פסח in טומאה. If only a minority is טמא מת, that minority brings פסח שני. The ruling here is surprising: the טמאי מתים get neither option and end up with no פסח at all. The זבין matter because a זב can never bring the פסח in טומאה; the permission to offer in impurity covers only טומאת מת.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was stated": introduces a teaching of the אמוראים
People with a זיבה discharge. Their impurity is never permitted for the פסח
People impure from contact with a dead body
One third of them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the two impure groups simply add up to a majority that can bring the פסח in טומאה. The זבין count differently for the first פסח than they do for the second. That is the whole point of this case.

phrases.english: It was stated: if a third of them were zavim,
and a third of them were pure,
and a third of them were impure from a corpse —
Rabbi Mani bar Pattish said:
those impure from a corpse do not perform [the Pesach]
neither the first nor the second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case connected to the same theme of impure majorities and minorities
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a split of thirds (זבין, pure, טמאי מתים), the טמאי מתים bring neither the first פסח nor פסח שני.

steps.title: Why the טמאי מתים cannot bring the first פסח
steps.stepSummary: For the first פסח, the זבין count together with the pure people, because a זב can never offer in טומאה. That makes the טמאי מתים a minority, and a minority may not bring the פסח in impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not bring the first פסח because the זבין are added to the pure side, since זבין cannot bring the פסח in impurity. So the טמאי מתים are a minority, and a minority does not bring the first פסח in impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of רבי מני בר פטיש's ruling: why the טמאי מתים miss the first פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that allows bringing the פסח in טומאה applies only when most of the people are טמא מת. The זבין are not part of that group, because their impurity is never permitted. So for this question they count on the side of the pure people. That leaves the טמאי מתים at one third, which is a minority, so they cannot bring the פסח on the first date.

keyTerms.meaning: Increased / added to the count of
A minority
On the first פסח (14 ניסן)
They do not perform

phrases.english: On the first they do not perform:
the zavim are added to the pure,
since they [zavim] do not perform in impurity,
so the corpse-impure are a minority —
and a minority does not perform on the first.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תשובה (answers the unstated question of why)
steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹן לָא עָבְדִי: הִגְדִּילוּ זָבִין עַל הַטְּהוֹרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the ruling in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the first פסח, the זבין count with the pure people, so the טמאי מתים are a minority and cannot offer in טומאה.

steps.title: Why the טמאי מתים also cannot bring פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: For פסח שני, the זבין now count together with the טמאי מתים, because both groups missed the first פסח. Together they make up a majority, and a majority is never sent to פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not bring the second פסח because the זבין join the טמאי מתים, since neither group brought the first פסח. Together they are the majority, and a majority is not pushed off to פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of the ruling, completing the reason the טמאי מתים lose both dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח שני exists only for a minority who missed the first פסח. For this question the counting changes: now the relevant grouping is 'everyone who did not bring the first פסח.' That group is the זבין plus the טמאי מתים, two thirds of the community and so a majority. A majority does not get פסח שני, so the טמאי מתים end up with nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Were joined / combined
A majority
The make-up פסח on 14 אייר
Are pushed off / deferred

steps.whatToRemember: The same זבין are counted with different groups depending on the question. For the first פסח, they side with the pure, since neither group is offering in impurity. For פסח שני, they side with the טמאי מתים, since both groups missed the first פסח. Because of this double counting, the טמאי מתים fall through the cracks.

phrases.english: On the second they do not perform:
the zavim are joined with the corpse-impure,
who did not perform on the first,
[so] they become the majority —
and a majority is not deferred to the second Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּשֵּׁנִי לָא עָבְדִי: נִצָּרְפוּ זָבִין עִם טְמֵאֵי מֵתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 3, explaining the second half of the ruling
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The טמאי מתים are a minority for the first פסח and part of a majority for פסח שני, so they bring neither.

steps.title: New משנה: the ציץ atones for an impure offering but not an impure person
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules on a פסח whose blood was already thrown before impurity was discovered. If the offering itself was impure, the ציץ atones and the פסח counts. If the person's body was impure, the ציץ does not atone.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a פסח's blood was thrown and afterward it became known that it was impure, the ציץ makes it acceptable. If the body of the person became impure, the ציץ does not make it acceptable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what happens when impurity is discovered only after the blood was already thrown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ, the golden plate on the כהן גדול's forehead, can make up after the fact for impurity in the offering itself, meaning its blood or meat. So the owner has fulfilled his פסח and does not need פסח שני. If instead the owner himself was impure, the ציץ does not help, and he must bring פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה: the new base text
The golden frontplate worn by the כהן גדול
Atones / makes the offering acceptable
Its blood was thrown on the מזבח
The body of the person bringing the offering

steps.confusionAlert: "שהוא טמא" in the first case refers to the offering, meaning its meat or blood. It does not refer to the person. The person is the separate case of "נטמא הגוף."

phrases.english: MISHNA: A Pesach whose blood was thrown
and afterward it became known that it was impure —
the frontplate atones.
[If] the body became impure —
the frontplate does not atone,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפֶּסַח שֶׁנִּזְרַק דָּמוֹ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹדַע שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציץ atones for impurity of the פסח offering, but not for impurity of the owner's body.

steps.title: The source rule: נזיר and פסח share the same ציץ limit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה grounds its ruling in an established teaching. For both a נזיר and someone bringing the פסח, the ציץ atones for impurity of the blood but not for impurity of the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the Sages said: for the נזיר and for one who brings the פסח, the ציץ atones for impurity of the blood, but the ציץ does not atone for impurity of the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason for its ruling by quoting a known rule that covers two cases, נזיר and פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזיר and the פסח are paired because in both, the person's own purity is central to the מצוה. A נזיר must be pure to complete his נזירות, and a person must be pure to be counted on the פסח. That is why the ציץ, which only fixes problems in the offering, cannot cover impurity of the person in either case.

keyTerms.meaning: "Because they said": introduces an established rule as the reason
A person who took a vow of נזירות
Impurity of the offering's blood
Impurity of the person's body

steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction between impurity of the offering and impurity of the person shapes the coming גמרא. The גמרא will ask what kind of bodily impurity is meant, and where this rule comes from.
steps.whatToRemember: The ציץ fixes problems in the קרבן, meaning its blood or meat. It does not fix problems in the person. For a נזיר and for the פסח, an impure person has not fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.english: because they said:
[for] the nazirite and one who performs the Pesach,
the frontplate atones for impurity of the blood,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל טוּמְאַת הַגּוּף.
phrases.english: and the frontplate does not atone for impurity of the body.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (cites an established rule as support)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ruling in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For both נזיר and פסח, the ציץ covers impurity of the blood but not impurity of the body.

steps.title: Hidden impurity of the deep: the ציץ still works
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with an exception. If the person became impure through טומאת התהום, the ציץ atones and the פסח is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he became impure with impurity of the deep, the ציץ atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a special exception. If the person was impure from a hidden source that nobody knew about, the offering is still accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 the משנה said the ציץ does not help when the person's body is impure. Here is an exception to that rule. If the person's impurity came from טומאת התהום, a source no one could have known about (like a buried grave discovered later), the offering is still accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity of the deep. A hidden source of impurity (e.g., a buried corpse) unknown to anyone until after the fact.
The golden frontplate worn by the כהן גדול, which atones for certain impurity in offerings.
Atones / makes the offering acceptable.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this contradicts Step 5. Body impurity is normally not covered by the ציץ. טומאת התהום is a special exception because the impurity was completely hidden.

phrases.english: If he became impure with impurity of the deep
phrases.notes: A hidden impurity, unknown to anyone at the time.

phrases.english: the frontplate atones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the משנה's rule that the ציץ does not atone for body impurity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For טומאת התהום, the ציץ atones even for the person's impurity.

steps.title: Reading the משנה closely: timing of discovery matters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that the ציץ atones only when the blood was thrown before the impurity was known. If the impurity was known first, it does not atone.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The reason it works is that the blood was thrown and only afterward the impurity became known. But if it became known first and then the blood was thrown, the ציץ does not atone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a precise inference from the wording of the משנה. This is a setup: the next step will challenge this inference with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the ציץ atones when the blood was 'already thrown' and then the impurity was discovered. The גמרא concludes that the order matters. If people knew the offering was impure and threw the blood anyway, the ציץ would not help.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is that… (introduces a precise inference from wording).
Was thrown. Refers to the throwing of the blood on the מזבח.
Became known.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The reason is that it was thrown
and afterward it became known,
but if it became known and afterward was thrown
it does not atone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by making an inference from the משנה's first clause about an impure offering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציץ atones only if the blood was thrown before the impurity became known.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the ציץ atones even when done on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It says the ציץ atones for impure blood, meat, and fat whether by mistake or on purpose, whether forced or willing, for an individual or the community. This seems to contradict the inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted it with a ברייתא: For what does the ציץ atone? For the blood, the meat, and the fat that became impure, whether by mistake or on purpose, whether by force or willingly, whether for an individual or for the community!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 8 with a ברייתא that seems to say the ציץ works even in deliberate cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ציץ atones even 'on purpose', then it should also work when people knew about the impurity and threw the blood anyway. That clashes with the inference that knowing first makes the ציץ fail.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it. Introduces a contradiction from another source.
By mistake, unknowingly.
On purpose, deliberately.
Under force, beyond one's control.

phrases.english: And they contrasted it:
For what does the frontplate atone?
For the blood and for the meat
and for the fat that became impure,
whether by mistake or on purpose,
whether by force or willingly,
whether for an individual or for the community!
phrases.notes: The exclamation marks this as a challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that the ציץ does not atone if the impurity was known before the זריקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the ציץ atones even in deliberate cases. So prior knowledge should not stop the ציץ from working.

steps.title: רבינא separates becoming impure from throwing the blood
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains the ברייתא's 'on purpose' as referring to the act of becoming impure. Throwing the blood while knowingly impure is not atoned. Throwing it by mistake is atoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Its becoming impure, whether by mistake or on purpose, is atoned. Its blood-throwing: by mistake, it is atoned; on purpose, it is not atoned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge. He shows that the ברייתא and the משנה are talking about two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate moments: when the offering became impure, and when the blood was thrown. The ברייתא's 'on purpose' is about the offering becoming impure, which the ציץ covers either way. The throwing must be done unknowingly, which matches the inference in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who offers the resolution.
Its impurity. The act of the offering becoming impure.
Its throwing. The throwing of the blood on the מזבח.
It was accepted / atoned.

steps.whatToRemember: The ציץ covers an offering that became impure, even deliberately. But if someone knowingly throws the blood of an impure offering, the ציץ does not help. Only a mistaken throwing is accepted.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Its impurity, whether by mistake or on purpose
phrases.notes: Refers to how the offering became impure.

phrases.english: it is accepted.
Its throwing: by mistake, it is accepted;
phrases.notes: Throwing the blood not knowing it was impure.

phrases.english: on purpose, it is not accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: טוּמְאָתוֹ בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג בֵּין בְּמֵזִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the ברייתא refers to how the offering became impure, while the inference refers to the throwing of the blood.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'on purpose' seemed to mean that even deliberately throwing impure blood is atoned.
steps.terutzMaskana: Impurity, whether by mistake or on purpose, is atoned. Throwing the blood is atoned only if done by mistake, so the inference from the משנה stands.

steps.title: רבי שילא: Throwing Is Always Accepted, but Becoming Impure on Purpose Is Not
steps.stepSummary: רבי שילא answers the contradiction differently from רבינא. Throwing the blood is accepted whether done by mistake or on purpose. Becoming impure is accepted only if it happened by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שילא said: As for throwing the blood, whether it was done by mistake or on purpose, it is accepted. As for its becoming impure, if that happened by mistake, it is accepted. If it happened on purpose, it is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שילא gives a second answer to the question from the ברייתא. He splits 'by mistake or on purpose' into two different moments: the throwing and the becoming impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא said that throwing the blood while knowing it was impure is not atoned. רבי שילא disagrees: even throwing it knowingly is accepted. For רבי שילא, the only thing that matters is how the offering became impure. If someone made it impure on purpose, the ציץ does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: By mistake, without knowing
On purpose, knowingly
Throwing the blood on the מזבח
It was accepted (the offering works)
Its becoming impure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two answers. רבינא says knowingly THROWING is a problem. רבי שילא says knowingly THROWING is fine, and only knowingly BECOMING IMPURE is a problem.

phrases.english: Rabbi Sheila said:

phrases.aramaic: זְרִיקָתוֹ, בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג בֵּין בְּמֵזִיד — הוּרְצָה.
phrases.english: Its throwing, whether by mistake or on purpose, is accepted.
phrases.notes: The 'on purpose' in the ברייתא applies to the throwing.

phrases.english: Its impurity, if it happened by mistake, is accepted;
if on purpose, it is not accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of step 9 that disagrees with רבינא's answer in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא by splitting 'mistake or on purpose' between the throwing and the becoming impure
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'on purpose' seemed to contradict the inference that the ציץ helps only when the impurity was not known before the throwing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Throwing is accepted even when done knowingly. Only impurity caused on purpose is not accepted.

steps.title: How רבי שילא Reads the ברייתא's Words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out how the ברייתא's 'by mistake or on purpose' fits רבי שילא's view. The offering became impure by mistake, and then it was thrown, either by mistake or on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what the ברייתא teaches, 'whether by mistake or on purpose,' means this: it became impure by mistake, and he threw it, whether by mistake or on purpose, and it is accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fits רבי שילא's view into the actual words of the ברייתא. It explains what the ברייתא's phrase 'by mistake or on purpose' is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not mean that becoming impure on purpose is fine. The impurity itself happened by mistake. The 'mistake or on purpose' describes only the throwing, which works either way.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
That which is taught
It became impure

phrases.english: But that which it teaches:
'whether by mistake or on purpose,'
this is what it means:
it became impure by mistake,

phrases.aramaic: וּזְרָקוֹ בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג בֵּין בְּמֵזִיד — הוּרְצָה.
phrases.english: and he threw it, whether by mistake or on purpose, and it is accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּקָתָנֵי בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג בֵּין בְּמֵזִיד הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי שילא's view from step 11 to the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'On purpose' might seem to include becoming impure on purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: The impurity was by mistake. Only the throwing may be either by mistake or on purpose.

steps.title: The Earlier Inference from the משנה Is Rejected
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי שילא, the משנה's words 'thrown and afterward it became known' do not teach a limit. The same law applies even if the impurity was known before the throwing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that which the משנה teaches, 'blood that was thrown and afterward it became known,' seems to mean that the reason it works is that it was thrown first and known afterward. If it was known first and thrown afterward, it would not work. But in fact, the same law applies even if it became known first and was thrown afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the inference from step 8 and rejects it according to רבי שילא. The ציץ helps even if the impurity was known before the throwing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 the גמרא learned from the משנה's wording that knowing first blocks the ציץ. Since רבי שילא says knowingly throwing is accepted, that inference cannot stand. The phrase 'thrown and afterward known' is just one example, not a requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: It became known
The reason is
The same law applies

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that one wording in a משנה can be read either as a limit or as just an example. Which reading is right depends on the answer you choose.

phrases.english: And that which it teaches:
'blood that was thrown and afterward it became known,'
suggesting the reason is that it was thrown and afterward it became known,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נוֹדַע וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִזְרָק — לָא,
phrases.english: but if it became known and afterward was thrown, not,
in fact, the same law applies
even if it became known and afterward was thrown.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּקָתָנֵי דָּם שֶׁנִּזְרַק וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי שילא's view from step 11 to cancel the inference made in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference from the משנה that the ציץ helps only when the impurity became known after the throwing
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's wording is only an example. Under רבי שילא, the ruling also holds when the impurity was known first.

steps.title: Why the משנה Still Said 'Thrown and Afterward Known'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה used the wording 'thrown and afterward known' so the first clause would match the last clause. In the last clause, about an impure body, the ציץ does not help even when the impurity became known only after the throwing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the reason the משנה says 'thrown and afterward known' is that it wanted to teach the last clause: 'if the body became impure, the ציץ does not atone.' There, even if the blood was thrown and only afterward it became known, the ציץ does not help. So it taught the first clause the same way too: 'thrown and afterward known.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the obvious question: if the wording is not a limit, why did the משנה use it? The answer is that it matches the wording of the last clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last clause, impurity of the body, 'thrown and afterward known' adds something important. Even in that easier case, the ציץ does not help. The משנה copied the same wording into the first clause for parallel style, not to set a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a teaching
The first clause of a teaching
The כהן גדול's golden frontplate
Brings atonement, makes the offering acceptable
Impurity of the person's body

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שילא: throwing the blood works whether done by mistake or on purpose. Only impurity caused on purpose blocks the ציץ. The משנה's phrase 'thrown and afterward known' is just there to match its last clause, about the impure body, where the ציץ does not help (except for טומאת התהום).

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי דְּקָתָנֵי נִזְרַק וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹדַע,
phrases.english: And that it teaches 'thrown and afterward it became known'
is because it wanted to teach the last clause:
'if the body became impure, the ציץ does not atone,'

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲפִילּוּ נִזְרַק וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹדַע — לָא,
phrases.english: where even if it was thrown and afterward it became known, it does not help,
so it taught the first clause also:
'thrown and afterward it became known.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unstated question raised by step 13: why the משנה used wording that is not a real condition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel wording: the first clause was phrased to match the last clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If knowing first does not matter, the משנה's wording 'thrown and afterward known' seems to have no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording is needed in the last clause, about the impure body, and was carried over to the first clause for parallel style.

steps.title: Does hidden impurity get the leniency for the priest too?
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה's case of טומאת התהום, רמי בר חמא asks a question. Does this leniency apply to the כהן doing the service, or only to the owners of the offering?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he became impure with hidden impurity, etc.' רמי בר חמא asked: The כהן who brings their offerings, is hidden impurity permitted for him, or not? Do we say the tradition about hidden impurity was taught only about the owners, and not about the כהן? Or perhaps it was taught about the offering itself, so there is no difference between the כהן and the owners?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה about טומאת התהום. רמי בר חמא asks whether that leniency covers the כהן who brings the offering, or only the person who owns it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency of טומאת התהום is known from a tradition (הלכה), not from a verse, so its exact limits are unclear. One option is that the tradition is about a person: the owner. The other option is that it is about the offering itself (the פסח or נזיר offering), so anyone involved, owner or כהן, would be covered.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity from a hidden source, like a buried corpse nobody knew about
He asked (raised an unresolved question)
The כהן who performs the service that makes the offering accepted
They learned it by oral tradition
There is no difference

steps.confusionAlert: This is still about the ציץ. The משנה itself says that for טומאת התהום "הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה": it is an exception to the rule that the ציץ does not cover bodily impurity. רמי בר חמא's question is how far this exception reaches. Does it cover only the owners, or the כהן too?

phrases.english: 'If he became impure with impurity of the deep, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה that opens the new discussion

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama asked:
The priest who brings their offerings,
phrases.notes: Their = the people bringing a פסח or a נזיר's offerings

phrases.aramaic: הוּתְּרָה לוֹ טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם, אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: is impurity of the deep permitted for him, or not?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן כִּי גְּמִירִי טוּמְאַת הַתְּהוֹם — בִּבְעָלִים,
phrases.english: Do we say that when they learned impurity of the deep, it was about the owners,
but about the priest, they did not learn it,
or perhaps they learned it about the offering itself,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא בְּכֹהֵן וְלָא שְׁנָא בִּבְעָלִים.
phrases.english: so there is no difference between the priest and the owners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from a different line of the משנה, after the discussion of when the ציץ covers an impure offering ended; it is still about how far the ציץ's leniency reaches
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the leniency of טומאת התהום is tied to the owner (a person) or to the offering (so it also covers the כהן)

steps.title: רבא brings a teaching that the leniency is only for corpse impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבא cites רבי חייא: the leniency of טומאת התהום applies only to impurity from a מת. He reads this as excluding hidden impurity from a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. רבי חייא taught: They said the rule of hidden impurity only about a corpse. What does 'corpse' come to exclude? Doesn't it come to exclude hidden impurity from a שרץ?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts building a proof from a ברייתא. It says the hidden-impurity leniency is only for corpse impurity, so hidden שרץ impurity gets no leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far רבא has only shown that hidden שרץ impurity is not forgiven. The question is who that rule could be about. If it cannot be about an owner, it must be about the כהן, and that would answer רמי בר חמא. The next steps check this.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: an introduction to a proof
To exclude
A dead creeping animal, which makes a person impure for one day
A corpse: the most severe impurity, lasting seven days

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear,
for Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
They did not state the rule of impurity of the deep
except for a corpse alone.
'A corpse' comes to exclude what?
Is it not to exclude impurity of the deep from a creeping animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רמי בר חמא's question from a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That the leniency of טומאת התהום applies to the כהן (to be shown by ruling out the owners)
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי חייא: the leniency is only for corpse impurity, which excludes hidden שרץ impurity

steps.title: Who is the case of hidden creeping-animal impurity about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבי חייא's exclusion is talking about. It starts by testing whether the case could be about the owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what case are we dealing with? If we say it is about the owners, which owner?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא begins checking, one by one, which person the exclusion of hidden שרץ impurity could refer to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on ruling out every kind of owner. The only offerings where טומאת התהום matters are the פסח and the נזיר's offerings. So the גמרא will test both kinds of owner.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
The owners of the offering

phrases.english: And what case are we dealing with?
If we say with the owners, then with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts testing the proof by defining the case of the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which owner the exclusion of hidden שרץ impurity could apply to

steps.title: It cannot be about a נזיר owner
steps.stepSummary: It cannot refer to a נזיר, because the Torah says only corpse impurity affects a נזיר. Excluding שרץ impurity for him would teach nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is about a נזיר, does שרץ impurity have any effect on him? The Torah says 'if a person dies beside him', meaning only a corpse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out the נזיר as the owner in רבי חייא's teaching. A שרץ never interrupts a נזיר's term anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a נזיר, only corpse impurity forces him to restart his term and bring offerings. Since a שרץ is meaningless for him whether hidden or known, there is nothing for רבי חייא to exclude in his case.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow to avoid wine, haircuts, and corpse impurity
Does it have any effect?
The Merciful One: the Torah

phrases.english: If with a nazirite, does it (creeping-animal impurity) have any effect on him?
'If a person dies beside him': so says the Merciful One.
phrases.notes: במדבר ו:ט: only corpse impurity affects a נזיר

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out the first kind of owner
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading רבי חייא's exclusion as being about a נזיר owner
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שרץ impurity has no effect on a נזיר at all, so there is nothing to exclude

steps.title: Perhaps it is about the owner of a פסח offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is about someone bringing a פסח. This works according to the view that we do not slaughter the פסח for people impure from a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about one bringing a פסח. This works well according to the one who says we do not slaughter and throw the blood for people impure from a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second kind of owner: a person bringing a פסח. It says this works under one view, and the next step will test the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the view that a person impure from a שרץ cannot have the פסח brought for him, it makes sense to say that hidden שרץ impurity is not forgiven either. Only corpse impurity gets the hidden-impurity leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: One who brings a קרבן פסח
This works well (according to one view)
We slaughter the offering and throw its blood

phrases.english: Rather, with one bringing the Paschal offering.
This works well according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין וְזוֹרְקִין עַל טְמֵאֵי שֶׁרֶץ.
phrases.english: we do not slaughter and throw the blood for those impure from a creeping animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the נזיר is ruled out, offers the פסח owner as the case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא could be about a פסח owner, at least under the view that the פסח is not slaughtered for someone impure from a שרץ

steps.title: Under the other view, known creeping-animal impurity is already allowed
steps.stepSummary: Under the view that we do slaughter the פסח for people impure from a שרץ, even known שרץ impurity is permitted. So hidden שרץ impurity is surely permitted, and רבי חייא could not be excluding it for the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says we do slaughter and throw the blood for people impure from a שרץ: if known impurity is permitted for him, isn't hidden impurity all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the פסח-owner reading fails under the second view. For him, even known שרץ impurity is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, a person impure from a שרץ can have his פסח brought, because he will immerse and be pure by nighttime when it is eaten. If known impurity is allowed, it makes no sense to forbid hidden impurity. So רבי חייא's exclusion cannot be about the owner here, which points to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Known impurity: the person knows he is impure
All the more so
Now (if this is true), introducing a 'how much more so' argument

steps.whatToRemember: The owner options keep failing: a נזיר never, and a פסח owner only under one view. This is pushing the גמרא toward reading רבי חייא as talking about the כהן, which would answer רמי בר חמא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a person impure from a שרץ eats the פסח while impure. Under this view, the offering is brought for him during the day, and by nightfall he has immersed and is pure for the eating.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
we do slaughter and throw the blood for those impure from a creeping animal,
now, if known impurity is permitted for him,
is impurity of the deep not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שׁוֹחֲטִין וְזוֹרְקִין עַל טְמֵאֵי שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the פסח-owner reading under the second view
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רבי חייא's ברייתא as being about a פסח owner
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if known שרץ impurity is permitted for the owner, hidden שרץ impurity must be too, so there is nothing to exclude for him

steps.title: So the ruling must be about the priest
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי חייא's exclusion cannot refer to the owners, it must refer to a כהן. This shows that hidden corpse impurity is permitted for a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it talking about a כהן? Learn from this that טומאת התהום was permitted for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's proof. The owners have been ruled out, so רבי חייא must be speaking about the כהן who brings the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 18-20 showed that the exclusion makes no sense for a נזיר or for a person bringing a פסח. The only option left is the כהן. If רבי חייא excludes hidden שרץ impurity for a כהן, then hidden corpse impurity must be permitted for him. That answers the original question.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest; here, the one doing the service
Learn from this; it is proven
Was permitted
Hidden impurity that nobody knew about (literally, 'impurity of the deep')

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about a priest?
And learn from this that it was permitted for him:
hidden impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after the owner options were ruled out in steps 18-20.
steps.raayaObject: Hidden corpse impurity is permitted for a כהן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's statement that the leniency applies only to impurity from a מת, read as being about the כהן.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it is about owners bringing a פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects the proof. רבי חייא may be speaking about owners bringing a פסח, and he is excluding hidden impurity from זיבה, not from שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: No. It is really about the owners and the פסח. The point is to exclude hidden impurity of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on רבא's proof. He shows that the ruling can still be about the owners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difficulty in step 20 came from assuming that רבי חייא was excluding שרץ impurity. רב יוסף says he was excluding hidden זיבה impurity, which is more severe. With that reading, the ruling fits the owners again, and nothing is proven about a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; in fact (keeps the original reading)
The owners of the offering
To exclude
An impure bodily discharge of a זב or זבה

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף does not change the people involved. He changes what kind of impurity is being excluded: זיבה instead of שרץ.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: No,
really it is about the owners, and about the Pesach.
And it comes to exclude hidden impurity of a discharge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 21 by rereading what רבי חייא excludes.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that רבי חייא must be speaking about a כהן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that the excluded impurity was שרץ. It could instead be זיבה, which fits the owners.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוסי's ruling on a זבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether hidden זיבה impurity is really not covered. It begins quoting רבי יוסי's ברייתא about a שומרת יום כנגד יום whose פסח was offered for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the ציץ not appease for hidden זיבה impurity? But it was taught: רבי יוסי says, a שומרת יום כנגד יום for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled the blood...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's answer. It starts quoting a ברייתא that seems to show hidden זיבה impurity is covered. The rest of the ברייתא comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף claimed that hidden זיבה impurity is not forgiven. The ברייתא describes a woman who might be a זבה, and a פסח was offered for her. The גמרא is setting up a ruling that her offering still counts, which would contradict רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Appeases; makes the offering acceptable (said of the ציץ)
But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradiction)
A woman who saw blood outside her normal time and must watch the next day to see whether she becomes a זבה
They sprinkled the blood of the offering

phrases.english: And for hidden impurity of a discharge, it does not appease?
But it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
A woman who keeps watch a day for a day
for whom they slaughtered and sprinkled the blood

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטוּמְאַת תְּהוֹם דְּזִיבָה לֹא מְרַצֶּה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's claim in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that hidden זיבה impurity is not forgiven.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's ברייתא seems to accept a פסח offered for a woman who has a hidden זיבה status. That suggests hidden זיבה impurity is covered.
